keyframe_review.note: 57,074 km2 (eastern Delta and the Levantine coast) for -1800..-1701. The Hyksos page dates 'gradual Canaanite settlement beginning there c. 1800 BC during the Twelfth Dynasty', 'a continuous Asiatic presence at Avaris for over 150 years before the beginning of Hyksos rule', and Hyksos rule from c. 1650 BC (infobox 'fl. c. 1650 - c. 1550 BC'). The Levantine coast is not shown to be Hyksos land on any page.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 87,492 km2 (Egypt, Jordan, Syria) is cut to the Egyptian part, the Fifteenth Dynasty shape of Memphis, the western Delta and Middle Egypt up to Cusae (lat 27.7) plus the eastern Delta round Avaris, and the one Levantine place the pages name, Sharuhen. The page: infobox area 'Lower Egypt and Middle Egypt, up to Cusae'; direct control 'probably limited to the eastern Nile delta'; the southern border was at Hermopolis and Cusae (the page's words, undated); Sharuhen (possibly Tell el-Ajjul) 'some scholars argue was a city in Canaan under Hyksos control'. The Fifteenth Dynasty page: territory 'may have included Canaan itself' (not drawn). Years -1700..-1651 belong to the Fourteenth Dynasty. fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): reduced to the Levantine part. The Fifteenth Dynasty page: 'The 15th Dynasty of Egypt was the first Hyksos dynasty, ruling from Avaris'; the Hyksos page calls the Hyksos 'the kings of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt'. Both dossiers drew the same Avaris kingdom (same Cliopatria shape, 31 scattered cells of one state in two colours), so the Egyptian land stays with fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt and this dossier keeps only Sharuhen, the one place the Hyksos page ('some scholars argue ... was a city in Canaan under Hyksos control') and the Fifteenth Dynasty page ('an area which may have included Canaan itself') give outside Egypt.

keyframe_review.note: 66,835 km2 in Jordan, Syria and Israel for -1500..-1401, a century after the Hyksos. The Ahmose I page has him complete 'his victory over the Hyksos by conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege'; no page shows a Hyksos power in the Levant afterwards. The Hyksos page notes only Hyksos-style pottery and scarabs continuing in the eastern Delta.

ledger.note: c. 1650 BC (undated): Sharuhen is a Hyksos stronghold. Ahmose I page: he 'completed his victory over the Hyksos by conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege'; the Hyksos page: 'some scholars argue was a city in Canaan under Hyksos control'. No year for its acquisition; set at the dynasty's start (c. 1650 BC, Hyksos infobox). Counterpart nobody (Canaanite local rule). fx-48 (3 Nov 2026): this is now the whole of the dossier. The Avaris foundation (replacing the Fourteenth Dynasty), the Memphis and Middle Egypt gain from the Thirteenth Dynasty and the Theban and Cusae contests are the fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt dossier's ledger/0-6, which draws the same kingdom; the Fifteenth Dynasty page: 'ruling from Avaris'.

wars.name: Theban-Hyksos war
wars.outcome: Seqenenre Tao 'started a series of wars against the Hyksos and perished in battle'; Kamose 'continued the war'; Ahmose I conquered Avaris in his fourth attack and then Sharuhen, and reunited Egypt.
wars.note: Years are the first clash at Thebes (c. 1630, Fifteenth Dynasty page) to the end of Hyksos rule (c. 1550). Dates conflict: the Hyksos page puts Kamose's campaign c. 1542 BC and Ahmose I's conquest of Avaris in his year 18 (c. 1532 BC); the Second Intermediate Period page puts Seqenenre c. 1549-1545 and Kamose c. 1545-1540. No siege or battle is dated on any page.

wars.name: Siege of Sharuhen
wars.outcome: Ahmose I 'completed his victory over the Hyksos by conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege.'
wars.note: Years are the three-year siege after Avaris (undated on the page); here counted from the dissolution year. Reviewer me-03-a: bounded to the dossier's end (-1550); the rest of the three-year siege belongs to new-kingdom-of-egypt's ledger.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders. The southern frontier at Cusae and Hermopolis is attested for the Hyksos and Theban kingdoms but not as a surveyed line; the Levantine stronghold at Sharuhen is a point, not a frontier.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Hyksos' (-1800..-1401; four shapes of 57k, 87k, 134k and 67k km2 in Egypt, Israel, Lebanon, Jordan and Syria) is far larger than any page supports: the Hyksos kingdom is Avaris, Lower Egypt and Middle Egypt up to Cusae (Hyksos page infobox), 'direct control probably limited to the eastern Nile delta', with one stronghold at Sharuhen. Shapes -1800 and -1500 are 'wrong'; -1700 and -1600 are cut to the Egyptian part and re-dated to the page's c. 1650-c. 1550 BC. DUPLICATE ROW: Cliopatria's 'Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt' (-1600..-1501, another batch, slug fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt) is the same dynasty (both infoboxes say Avaris, 1650 to c. 1550 BC; the Hyksos infobox is headed 'Hyksos (Fifteenth Dynasty)'); its shape of 34,496 km2 (Memphis, western Delta, Middle Egypt to lat 27.7) is used here as the Egyptian core, so the two dossiers describe one state and should be merged or one demoted by the orchestrator; likewise the Sixteenth Dynasty shape (Cliopatria puts it in the Delta, the pages put it at Thebes). DATE CONFLICTS: infobox c. 1550 BC end vs Ahmose I's conquest in year 18 (c. 1532 BC, Schneider) vs Khamudi 'c. 1550-1540' vs Kamose's campaign 'c. 1542 BC' (Hyksos page) or 'c. 1555-1550' (Kamose page) or 'c. 1545-1540' (Second Intermediate Period page); Ahmose I's own reign has four dates on his page (1570-1546, 1560-1537, 1551-1527, 1539-1514 BC) and 'c. 1549-1524 BC' on the Hyksos page. The dossier uses the infobox c. 1550 BC end, so a reviewer should expect the real fall of Avaris up to two decades later. NOT DRAWN: Canaan-wide or Syria-wide Hyksos power (the Fifteenth Dynasty page says only 'may have included Canaan itself'; Kamose calls Apophis 'Chieftain of Retjenu' (undated)); Thebes as a Hyksos vassal (the Hyksos page: Ryholt calls it 'a baseless assumption'); Khyan's conquest of 'the whole of Egypt' (undated, Fifteenth Dynasty page); Cyprus trade and Khyan's objects abroad. No ruler strip: the pages give no reign dates for the Hyksos kings except Apophis 'c. 1590?-1550' and Khamudi 'c. 1550-1540'. States needed from other groups: fourteenth-dynasty-of-egypt (Avaris, c. 1700-1650 BC, predecessor), the Abydos Dynasty (c. 1640-1620), kingdom of Kerma/Kush. Gazetteer names needed: Sharuhen (Tell el-Ajjul near Gaza; a radius at lat 31.5 lon 34.47 is used), Cusae (lat 27.43 lon 30.82; a radius at 27.6 is used), Retjenu.
